title: SketchPolymer: Estimate Per-item Tail Quantile Using One Sketch

problem.claim: Estimating distribution quantiles, particularly tail quantiles, is a problem in data stream models.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes SketchPolymer, a sketch for estimating per-item tail quantiles.
SketchPolymer uses Early Filtration to filter infrequent items and VSS to reduce error.
The authors implement SketchPolymer on P4 and FPGA platforms.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe SketchPolymer as a novel sketch.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that SketchPolymer's accuracy is on average 32.67 times better than state-of-the-art techniques.
The authors report deployment-flexibility verification through implementations on P4 and FPGA platforms.
The authors report that all code is available on GitHub.

narrative_sequence.summary: Quantile estimation, especially for tail distributions, is a topic of interest in data stream models.
The paper proposes SketchPolymer for per-item tail-quantile estimation and describes Early Filtration and VSS as its main techniques.
The authors report improved accuracy, implementations on P4 and FPGA platforms, and publicly available code.

source_observation.claim: The method filters infrequent items and applies a technique intended to reduce error.

interpretation.claim: Separating infrequent-item filtering from error reduction may help manage per-item tail-quantile estimation costs and accuracy.

application.claim: A streaming quantile system could consider frequency-based filtering together with a dedicated error-reduction technique.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the conditions under which these techniques provide the reported benefits.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the data distributions, workloads, baselines, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not describe the SketchPolymer data structure, algorithms, memory usage, or error guarantees.
The abstract does not provide platform implementation details or deployment measurements.
